C-4.Name: Fix sidebar rename of open files: missing RENAME_IF_NEEDED action
C-4.Summary: store/project.js RENAME_IN_SIDEBAR calls editorStore.RENAME_IF_NEEDED({src, dest}) — an action that does not exist in the editor store. Renaming a file with an open tab from the sidebar rejects with a TypeError inside the rename(...).then callback (unhandled rejection), the tab keeps the old pathname/filename, and its per-file watcher stays keyed to the old path (external changes to the renamed file stop live-reloading). Discovered during C-2 recon; planned here so it is not forgotten. NOT IMPLEMENTED YET — this is a planning artifact only.

Problem.Description: Sidebar rename of an open file breaks the open tab: TypeError (RENAME_IF_NEEDED is not a function), stale tab pathname, stale watcher subscription.
Problem.RootCause: project.js:529 references a v1-era action name that was never ported into the Pinia editor store.
Problem.Evidence: grep RENAME_IF_NEEDED across src/renderer/src → single call site in store/project.js RENAME_IN_SIDEBAR; no definition anywhere.

Goals.R-1: Implement editor-store action RENAME_IF_NEEDED({src, dest}): find tabs whose pathname matches src (window.fileUtils.isSamePathSync), update pathname + filename to dest, and notify the editor surface via the existing bus channel used by RENAME_FILE (bus.emit('rename')) so the tab title and source-code path follow.
Goals.R-2: Move the per-file watcher subscription: _unsubscribeFileWatch(src) + _subscribeFileWatch(dest) for each affected tab (C-2 pending-marker protocol makes this race-safe). Drop liveReloadGenerations for src.
Goals.R-3: No unhandled rejection remains in RENAME_IN_SIDEBAR; failure of the store action must surface via notice.notify like other sidebar errors.
Goals.R-4: Unit tests: rename with one open tab (title/path/watcher follow), rename with no open tab (no-op), rename with two tabs on the same file, watcher resubscription asserted via the ipcWatch mock.

Constraints.Constraint: Reuse the C-2 watch-subscribe protocol; do not introduce a second subscription mechanism.
Match v1 semantics: only tabs of the renamed file move; other tabs untouched.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Bulk rename, undo of rename, or directory rename propagation to open tabs (separate concerns if ever needed).

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Sidebar rename of an open file updates the tab (pathname, filename, tab title) with zero console errors.
After rename, an external edit of the NEW path live-reloads the tab and an external edit of the OLD path does nothing.
Renderer suites green; new tests cover all four R-4 scenarios.

AffectedAreas.M-032: editor store: new RENAME_IF_NEEDED action + watcher move (store/editor.js)

C-4.VerificationIntent: Unit tests in tests/renderer/store/editor-deep*.test.js + project.test.ts pinning the four scenarios; runtime smoke: rename an open file in the sidebar of the live app, externally edit the renamed file, confirm BLOCK_LIVE_RELOAD for the new path in stderr.

Amendment.Reason: Live WKWebView smoke (T-004) findings; fixed under "закрывай 1-3" (user, 2026-10-13).
Amendment.Item: Data loss fixed (51537e8b): macOS FSEvents reports a rename as Modify(Name), which the project watcher forwards as 'change', not 'add'. The echo guard only covered 'add', so with liveReload on a dirty renamed tab was re-read from disk. Every add/change echo for the new path inside the 2 s window is now ignored.

Tree fixed (51537e8b): the project watcher's 'modify' handler ignored tree shape, so after a sidebar rename or an external mv the tree kept the old node. A vanished path now leaves the tree (and marks its tab), and a new markdown file joins it.

Blocker fixed (434ae3b6, M-009): native context-menu clicks were intermittently lost — the item MenuEvent reached capture_context_menu_selection after popup_at had returned and the pending entry was gone, so sidebar Rename did nothing. The popup command now waits up to 250 ms for the late selection. This is the root cause of the transient "context menu / copy does nothing" report of 2026-10-13.
